messages.subject: Is the linked brush example app supposed to work currently?
messages.subject_clean: Is the linked brush example app supposed to work currently?
messages.body_plain:
Dear ggvis team,

I have started to evaluate ggvis for a new project and I really like what I have seen and tried so far.

One thing I couldn't make work is the linked brush example app (ggvis <https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis> / demo <https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/tree/master/demo> / apps <https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/tree/master/demo/apps> / brush-linked <https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/tree/master/demo/apps/brush-linked> /). Layer_brush() and brush_delay are gone. Thus I have modified the brush reactive from

  gv1 <- reactive({
    ggvis(diamonds, props(x = ~carat, y = ~price)) +
      mark_symbol(props(fill.brush := "red", fillOpacity := 0.8, key := ~id)) +
      layer_brush() +
      opts(width = 300, height = 300, brush_delay = 100)
  })

into

  gv1 <- reactive({
   lb <- linked_brush(keys = 1:nrow(diamonds))
    ggvis(diamonds, props(x = ~carat, y = ~price)) +
      mark_symbol(props(fill.brush := "red", fillOpacity := 0.8, key := ~id)) +
      lb$brush_handler() +
      opts(width = 300, height = 300)
  })

following the syntax from the linked_brush help. This makes the app load and to display the brush, but the brush does not seem to trigger any events. Is this supposed to work already?

Thanks a lot, and good luck with ggvis. It looks very promising already.

Thomas

messages.subject: Philosophical question about tourr
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have spent some time being impressed/hypnotized by the tourr demo.

Looking at the code, I see it uses reactive calls in conjunction with shiny.

The demo works well self-contained on my laptop.

Would it / could it work well as a web-deployed shiny app? Or would it / could it get bogged down (esp. with many points) in server/client communications, updating for each frame?

This is not a feature request or suggestion - you guys are busy enough. It's just me trying to sort out how all this stuff might be able to work together for the foreseeable future.

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
It may get bogged down, but we still have a lot of optimisation to do.
ggvis is always going to be faster when used locally, but I think most
common that don't involve sending heaps of data around should be fine
remotely as well.

Hadley

messages.subject: ggvis 0.1
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

We're pleased to announce the 0.1 release of ggvis. ggvis is the next iteration of ggplot2, and it adds new capabilities like interactivity, dynamic updates, and rendering in a web browser.

You're receiving this email because you are an active member of the ggplot2 community, an early user of ggvis. This is an invitation to start using ggvis, participate in the mailing list (https://groups.google.com/group/ggvis) and give feedback via the GitHub issue tracker (https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues).

There is online documentation at http://ggvis.rstudio.com/

To install ggvis, run the following code in R:
if(!require('devtools') || packageVersion('devtools') < 1.4) {
  install.packages('devtools')
}
devtools::install_github(c("hadley/testthat", "rstudio/shiny", "rstudio/ggvis"))

Version 0.1 of ggvis is an alpha release, so please keep in mind that the API is still subject to change. We strongly suggest not using for it for production purposes at this time.

Thanks for your help!
Winston Chang and Hadley Wickham

messages.subject_clean: question regarding properties in custom style
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Firstly, big congrats to the release of ggvis 0.1.

Secondly, I have a question regarding properties in axis. The same question was also mentioned before.
I used ggvis 0.1 and tried the code presented on the ggvis website (http://ggvis.rstudio.com/axes-legends.html#custom-styles)
ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg)) +
  mark_symbol() +
  guide_axis("x", properties = list(
    axis = props(stroke = "red", strokeWidth = 5),
